You can notice I rushed the first answer and choose to take more room next time. That is more actionable than I am hopeless. Support also makes room to acknowledge what did work, so your picture of an attempt is more complete. You remain responsible for your choices without treating yourself as an enemy.

sections.narration:
Welcome. Today we are exploring Stop Standing Against Yourself. After a difficult answer, your internal voice says: Why are you still doing this? You know better. The next answer begins with an argument already taking place inside you.

In this session, we will recognise a personal attack, keep useful information, and choose a supportive next step. I will explain the idea, show a visual example, and invite you to try it in a small experience of your own. You can ask me a question or switch to reading at any point. We will finish by choosing what, if anything, you want to take into a real conversation.

sections.narration: You can recognise something difficult without becoming your own opponent. Supporting yourself means describing the task and choosing a useful response, rather than adding an attack on the person doing it. The attack may sound motivating because it is urgent. Notice whether it actually helps you participate in the next moment, or asks you to spend more energy defending yourself.

sections.narration:
After a difficult answer, your internal voice says: Why are you still doing this? You know better. The next answer begins with an argument already taking place inside you.

A supportive response can be honest. You can say that answer was hard, I wanted more time, or I rushed. Support is not a claim that every attempt was wonderful. It is the decision to stay on your own side while you work with what happened. That leaves room for both learning and dignity.

You remain responsible for your choices without treating yourself as an enemy.

Changed, unchanged or uncertain experiences are all information.

sections.narration: Support does not require positive self-talk you do not believe. A factual sentence such as I can take a moment is enough. If an attacking thought returns, you do not need to punish yourself for having it. A changed, unchanged or uncertain experience is information, not a grade. You do not have to report relief for this attempt to count as exploration.

sections.narration: Keep one believable supportive phrase available for your next conversation. Use it as help, not as a compulsory ritual. During focused practice, you can deliberately explore this one tool. In an everyday conversation, give most of your attention to the message and the other person. A familiar support can be available if it helps; you do not have to monitor the tool throughout the exchange.
